# BMS / DJMax Keysound Slicer UX audit

**Research note.** This is an evidence-led audit of pages actually retrieved on 2026-09-18. Where a limit or behaviour was not published by a retrieved source, it is marked **not established**, rather than inferred. Japanese/Korean passages are translated inline.

## 1. Comparison table

| Tool | Workflow (observed) | Top 3 pain points / limits | Max slices / snap | Export method |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Sayaslicer** | Open/drag audio; add markers; optionally import BMHelper/MIDI markers; tune offset/snap; preview; copy BMSE/iBMSC data; export keysounds and/or keysound list; save project. README explicitly positions it as a WoslicerII replacement. [GitHub README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer) | 1) Still an export step. 2) Zero-crossing moves markers, which can break iBMSC paste/save (missing keysounds or gamemode change); workaround is BMSE clipboard, which rounds to 1/192. 3) Partial BPM-change support is described as “a bit hackish”; proper BPM/grid support is still planned. [README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer) | Arbitrary snap **1/1–1/192**; no maximum slice count published. [README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer) | `M` exports keysounds; BMSE clipboard, iBMSC clipboard, keysound-list clipboard/BMS append. [README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer) |
| **Woslicer II / III** | Prepare WAV; set BPM/offset; click cut points; output many WAVs; output clipboard/wos metadata; import/define WAVs in BMSE; paste sequence. BMHelper route adds MIDI export → DAW render → copy cut positions → Woslicer clipboard import → total output. [Purureko guide](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/) [BMHelper guide](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html) | 1) Manual multi-app ceremony and repeated per-part work. 2) File order matters: BMSE definitions follow Explorer ordering and the drag selection, so both start positions must be correct. 3) Tail/last-slice housekeeping: guide deletes a silent final slice; long sounds must be split below one minute for LR2 ranking. [Purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/) [Woslicer III guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3) | Woslicer III guide documents grid **up to 192 per bar**; no maximum number of markers published. [Woslicer III guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3) | “Total output” WAVs plus clipboard sequence; Woslicer III also writes `.wos` marker/settings data. [Woslicer III guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3) |
| **BMHelper + Mid2BMS** | Export MIDI from DAW → BMHelper separates/normalizes notes → render generated MIDI to WAV → slice at copied cut positions; Mid2BMS alternative: configure mode/start definition/interval/timebase, render MIDI, WaveSplitter uses tail threshold/silence detection, rename generated `.txt` to `.bms`, test in viewer. [BMHelper](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html) [Mid2BMS workflow](https://note.com/nakaiankow/n/n03caf5d703f9) | 1) DAW/MIDI round trip is mandatory for the MIDI route. 2) Interval is in beats and therefore BPM-dependent; too long makes WAVs long, too short overlaps tails/heads. 3) TailCut/silence detection has no universal optimum; too small/large changes slice count. [Mid2BMS workflow](https://note.com/nakaiankow/n/n03caf5d703f9) | Mid2BMS uses two-character base-36 start definitions (`01…zz`) in the guide; no snap denominator/max-slice value established. [Mid2BMS workflow](https://note.com/nakaiankow/n/n03caf5d703f9) | Generated WAV/BMS/clipboard-like placement data; final guide recommends converting WAV to OGG separately. [Mid2BMS workflow](https://note.com/nakaiankow/n/n03caf5d703f9) |
| **PTSEQUENCER** | No reliable workflow or settings page was retrieved in this run. | The often-repeated “2047 keysound limit” could not be attributed to a retrieved PTSEQUENCER source; do not implement it as a PTSEQUENCER-specific fact. | Not established. | Not established. |
| **sound-slicer** | Keep original project files and `.txt` beside source WAV; output slices into a `wav` subfolder alongside BMS. Rhythmic mode slices every MIDI event; melodic mode groups by note/length/velocity, renders a reorganized MIDI, then slices and pastes generated clipboard data. [README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer) | Rhythmic mode can produce one slice per 1,000 MIDI notes and “may result in slight gaps”; melodic mode requires another audio-app render; both modes do **not support BPM changes**. [README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer) | No snap control or max slice count published. | WAV slices plus generated BMS clipboard text. [README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer) |

## 2. Problem inventory

### Timeline

| Severity | Problem / user consequence | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **P0** | Timing is split across BPM/grid coordinates and audio milliseconds. BPM changes are a major failure point: a BMS guide says “BPM changes make slicing extremely difficult”; sound-slicer explicitly does not support them; Sayaslicer calls its support partial/hackish and lists proper grid display as planned. | [BMS guide](https://note.com/nakaiankow/n/n03caf5d703f9), [sound-slicer README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer), [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer) |
| **P1** | Users align by visually comparing a waveform and a bar/beat cursor, then auditioning. The Woslicer III guide says to align the waveform head to the orange line and use `P`; long audio can delay playback, so users pre-cut the next bar to speed loading. | [Woslicer III guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3) |
| **P1** | Reverb tails and final boundaries are manual judgement. A documented example extends the final cut to account for a snare tail, then deletes the resulting silent final WAV. | [Woslicer III guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3) |
| **P1** | Zero-crossing improves click resistance but changes timing coordinates. The documented iBMSC failure mode is missing keysounds or gamemode change after save. | [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer) |

### Interface / workflow

| Severity | Problem / user consequence | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **P0** | Traditional workflow is destructive and multi-stage: render, split hundreds of WAVs, define files, paste sequence, then test. Guides call the sound-cutting stage the most troublesome and repeat it for each part. | [Purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/), [Woslicer III guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3) |
| **P1** | Clipboard is a fragile integration boundary. BMHelper data disappears if BMHelper is closed; sequence must be pasted at the current measure and BGM lane; definitions must begin at the correct index. | [BMHelper guide](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html) |
| **P1** | File-management errors silently mis-map audio: BMSE uses Explorer ordering and the selected starting file; the guide explicitly warns to select the head in both places. | [Purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/) |
| **P1** | Base-36/base-62 compatibility is a real boundary, not merely UI polish. NamuWiki reports classic BMS `01–ZZ` as 1,295 definitions and BMSE’s 2024 base-62 experiment as 3,843; Sayaslicer therefore exposes a toggleable base-62 BMSE clipboard mode and warns that BMSE rounds to 192nd. | [NamuWiki key sound](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C), [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer) |
| **P2** | BMHelper has a documented clipboard-definition defect: its beta guide says the copy button failed to insert line breaks, recommending copying the text area instead. | [BMHelper guide](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html) |

### Settings

| Severity | Problem / user consequence | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **P1** | Users tune offset/“ずらし” by comparing parts because rendered files may contain leading silence; guides recommend reusing a measured offset across parts. | [Woslicer III guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3) |
| **P1** | Fade and noise-gate/tail thresholds are subjective. Woslicer III exposes fade and noise gate; Mid2BMS exposes TailCut Threshold and silence-detection time, with explicit warnings that either extreme changes results. | [Woslicer III guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3), [Mid2BMS workflow](https://note.com/nakaiankow/n/n03caf5d703f9) |
| **P1** | Snap precision differs by interchange format: iBMSC allows arbitrary resolution, while BMSE clipboard rounds to 1/192. A marker can sound right but serialize wrong. | [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer) |
| **P2** | Normalization was not evidenced in the retrieved slicer docs; it should not be assumed as an existing setting. | No reliable retrieved claim; treat as a product gap to validate |

### Backend / output

| Severity | Problem / user consequence | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **P0** | Exporting physical files creates naming, ordering, definition-count, and cleanup risk. Woslicer outputs numbered files; users must manually define them and later convert WAV to OGG. | [Woslicer III guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3), [Mid2BMS workflow](https://note.com/nakaiankow/n/n03caf5d703f9) |
| **P0** | BMS’s historical definition ceiling constrains dense charts: 1,295 for base-36; BMSE’s newer base-62 path is 3,843 but requires compatible players/tools. | [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C), [BMSE base-62 article](https://manbow.nothing.sh/event/event.cgi?action=More_def&num=1&event=143) |
| **P1** | One-definition simultaneous playback and one-minute ranking rule shape the audio: the BMS guide says a definition cannot play simultaneously in most players and no defined sound may be one minute or longer for ranking submission. | [BMS guide](https://note.com/nakaiankow/n/n03caf5d703f9) |
| **P1** | Traditional reuse is manual/heuristic. sound-slicer’s melodic mode reduces 500 bass notes to 10 reusable slices by grouping note/length/velocity, while rhythmic mode deliberately keeps all events. | [sound-slicer README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer) |
| **P2** | Platform reliability is part of UX: Sayaslicer’s closed issues include Linux preview crashes due to PortAudio, >2GB load failure, macOS launch trouble, and text enlargement request. These are resolved/closed, but are useful regression-test cases. | [closed issues](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aclosed) |

## 3. What Sayaslicer did right vs Woslicer — keep these

**Keep from Sayaslicer:** arbitrary 1/1–1/192 snapping; explicit BMSE and iBMSC clipboard paths; base-62 toggle; project save/load; marker copy/paste; undo/redo; drag/drop; offset; configurable silent-tail removal; zero-crossing; keysound-list export; keyboard-first navigation; and multi-language support. These are all explicitly documented, not inferred. [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer)

**Keep from Woslicer:** the direct manipulation mental model—waveform, BPM, offset, fade, noise gate, grid, click-to-add cuts, audition, and one-button total output—is compact and understandable. Woslicer III’s mouse-first workflow is specifically preferred over II by one guide author, while the Woslicer ecosystem remains valuable because BMHelper can hand it cut positions via clipboard. [Purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/) [Woslicer III guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3)

**Do not copy:** the hidden coupling between Explorer order, definition start index, clipboard lifetime, and current BMSE measure/lane; or the need to delete a silent last file and convert hundreds of WAVs afterward. [BMHelper](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html) [Purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)

## 4. Top 10 recommendations for DJMax Studio

1. **P0 — Make slices non-destructive by default.** Store `{sourceFile,startMs,endMs}` and defer WAV/OGG export until finalize; this directly removes the render/split/rename/import ceremony documented by Woslicer and Mid2BMS. [Purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/) [Mid2BMS workflow](https://note.com/nakaiankow/n/n03caf5d703f9)
2. **P0 — Ship the proposed dual timeline.** Put waveform/ms on the lower ruler and Studio chart/bar/beat on the upper ruler, with one synchronized playhead. BPM changes are the clearest cross-tool failure, and Sayaslicer still lists proper BPM/grid support as future work. [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer) [BMS guide](https://note.com/nakaiankow/n/n03caf5d703f9)
3. **P0 — Make “Import to Studio” transactional and reversible.** Slices should instantiate notes plus a link back to the virtual slice; edits must round-trip without clipboard, Explorer ordering, or current-measure state. Those hidden state dependencies are explicitly documented in BMHelper/BMSE workflows. [BMHelper](https://w.atwiki.jp/coolnaurl/pages/19.html) [Purureko](https://purureko.com/etc/post-1704/)
4. **P0 — Add compatibility-aware export profiles: BMS base-36, BMS base-62, RESPECT, TECHNIKA.** Show definition budget and refuse/offer reuse when limits are exceeded; preserve a lossless internal ID. BMS’s 1,295/3,843 split is documented, and DJMAX-family key-sound handling has different interruption/reuse history. [NamuWiki](https://en.namu.wiki/w/%ED%82%A4%EC%9D%8C) [BMSE base-62 article](https://manbow.nothing.sh/event/event.cgi?action=More_def&num=1&event=143)
5. **P1 — Make snap explicit and per-slice overridable.** Offer 1/4…1/192 plus free-ms, show the quantization delta, and never silently move a zero-cross marker. This addresses Sayaslicer’s documented zero-cross/iBMSC incompatibility. [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer)
6. **P1 — Add safe zero-crossing with preview and policy.** “Move boundary to zero cross” should show before/after ms, permit per-slice off, and optionally preserve chart time while applying a microfade. The source documents click reduction but also timing/clipboard breakage. [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer)
7. **P1 — Build a Slice Library with reuse/deduplication.** Show source, start/end, duration, tail policy, export status, and all notes using it; offer melodic-style reuse but retain an explicit “unique slice” option. sound-slicer demonstrates both reuse (melodic) and one-event-per-slice (rhythmic). [sound-slicer README](https://github.com/dtinth/sound-slicer)
8. **P1 — Per-slice tail tools, not global destructive processing.** Draft slice, fade, zero-X, normalize, tail threshold and audition should be editable per slice and undoable. Existing guides show that tails and thresholds require part-specific judgement. [Woslicer III guide](https://spirea3cross.wixsite.com/bmstukuru2020/how-to-make3) [Mid2BMS workflow](https://note.com/nakaiankow/n/n03caf5d703f9)
9. **P1 — Make keyboard operation discoverable and context-safe.** Keep Sayaslicer’s shortcuts (Z/C/V/B/K/M/P, arrows, Ctrl-Z/Y), add a shortcut overlay, and ensure preview/auto-advance never changes selection invisibly. [Sayaslicer README](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer)
10. **P2 — Add preflight and regression fixtures.** Before finalize, detect >1-minute slices, orphan notes, silent tails, duplicate/over-budget definitions, BPM/grid mismatch, unsupported format, and round-trip differences; test Linux preview, >2GB files, macOS launch, arbitrary-resolution paste, and base-62. These correspond to documented BMS rules and Sayaslicer issue history. [BMS guide](https://note.com/nakaiankow/n/n03caf5d703f9) [closed issues](https://github.com/SayakaIsBaka/sayaslicer/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aclosed)
